title: the
parentNote: Today is different from every day so far: "the" is not sounded out, it is remembered. English kept a handful of its oldest and commonest words spelled the way people wrote them hundreds of years ago, and "the" is the commonest of the lot — sounding it out honestly would give you "tuh-huh-eh", which is nobody's word. So we teach it whole, the way you learn a face. There are only about forty words like this in the whole language and they come in slowly, one day at a time; everything else your child will ever read really can be sounded out. If they start to sound it out, stop them gently and just say it: this is the one place where guessing from memory is the right answer.

activities.sentence: The cat sat in the van.
activities.prompt: Do not sound this one out. It is a word we just know by sight: the.
No sounding out. Look at it and say it: the.
The word the starts with these two letters, but it does not obey them. Find the buzzy pair anyway.
Back to words we can sound out. Two teams, three sounds.
Tongue out and buzzing at the front.
Two letter teams that look alike. One buzzes, one puffs.
Does the start stop quickly, or go on and on?

activities.text: The chick sat with the fat cat.

activities.prompt: The word the turns up twice in this line. You will see it in nearly every line from now on.
